rows.note: Control: `with map "Role::$_", qw(Alpha Beta)` — the EXPRESSION-form template map folds statically; goto-def on the qw element Alpha reaches the role package. Pins that the fold itself works so the block-form rows isolate the callback-shape gap.

`with map { "Role::$_" } qw(Alpha Beta)` — BLOCK form of the same template map (at least as idiomatic as the expression form). CST: callback is a real `block` node wrapping an expression_statement with the same interpolated template; the folder must descend into the block tail.
Second qw element of the block-form map — pins that the fold produces one parent per list element with per-element spans, not just the first.

`with map { my $n = "Role::$_"; $n } qw(Alpha Beta)` — multi-statement block whose tail is a lexical bound once to the template. Perl returns the block's last expression; the fold must chase the single `my $n = TEMPLATE` binding to the template rather than pattern-matching a literal tail.
